text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Gorica Gajevic, general secretary to the Socialist Party of Serbia, received the delegation of Russian Duma on Monday and underlined that victory of the left, democratic and patriotic forces on Serbian elections was undisputable and recognised by international community.
- A group of 17 economists warned economy was facing collapse and demanded urgent and radical economic reforms.
- Belgrade's first municipal court annulled city's electoral comission ruling on opposition victory at November 17 local elections.
- West stepping up pressure on Belgrade regime, French Foreign Minister de Charette calls on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to recognise election results.
- Zajedno (Together) coalition calls on citizens to protest after Radio Television Serbia prime time news programme at 19.30 (1830 GMT).

- U.S. State Department delivered protest to the Yugoslav government over use of force against the people demonstrating peacefully and warned it (Belgrade) could not hope to attract international support if it continued to use force against innocent civilians.
- Yugoslav and Montengrin bar associations protest over violation of basic citizens' rights and annulment of election results.
- States emerged from former Yugoslavia to meet on February 17 in Brussels to discuss succession issues.
- Yugoslavia estimates current maize surplus at about two million tonnes.

- Minister coordinator in Serbian government Dragan Tomic said that unfavourable developments in the country (citizens' protests) must be stopped as soon as possible as they threaten "favourable" possibilities for cooperation with other countries.
- Serbian government plans spring sowing on 2.3 million hectares out of which 1.4 million hectares will be under maize.
